report:
The argument establishes the stated restricted theorem for moving logarithmic ordinary references on P¹ × Y, with any fixed compact Hermitian second factor and uniformly varying continuous factored densities. It satisfies the singular-reference/varying-data alternative in the completion criteria. These densities are bounded; this does not establish selection for general L¹ data or close the unrestricted S05 programme.

The geometry and model calculation check out independently. The horizontal-degree-two component of ddᶜθ is (ddᶜb)∧κ, which is nonzero because a nonconstant smooth function on P¹ cannot be harmonic. Other horizontal degrees cannot cancel it. On the curve, convexity of the radial profile, the terminal slope bound a, and tangency to K log(1+eˢ) give exactly the displayed φ. Its derivative agrees across the tangent circle, so there is no circle atom. Its horizontal non-pluripolar mass is K·R/(1+R)=a. Restricting each product competitor to a curve slice after adding an exact horizontal correction and a sufficiently large vertical quadratic proves the full-product envelope bound without symmetry assumptions on Y. The explicit tangent potential supplies the reverse inequality. The smaller-background competitor also works: δθ+ddᶜψ is positive whenever δ>d/(a+d).

Divisor removal is valid for θ-psh v≼ψ. The upper comparison makes r=v−ψ locally bounded above near D. The removable-extension theorem applies to r plus a strict local quadratic. Positivity of η+ddᶜr then follows separately off D and on D: on D, its matrix-measure restriction equals that of the positive corrected Hessian because smooth corrections assign D zero measure. Canonical representatives give genuine equality v=ψ+r, including poles. Locality and the absence of pluripolar mass identify the two non-pluripolar products globally, including additional poles of r. The extension and envelope prerequisites were checked in [Demailly’s manuscript](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf).

Existence and greatestness cover the entire advertised singular subsolution class. Here η is strictly positive, a sufficiently negative constant is a global strict barrier, and gσ=e^{σψ}f is bounded, nonnegative and nonzero despite vanishing on D. Thus the positive-exponent existence theorem applies for every σ>0, without a bounded mass property assumption. For an arbitrary residual subsolution r, choose a finite truncation level strictly below the bounded floor Rσ−M. The ordered bounded maximum inequality then proves that max(r,Rσ−M) is an exponential subsolution, including its equality set. On {Rσ<max(r,Rσ−M)−ε}, the required strict measure ratio is e^{−σε}<1. Both compared potentials are bounded and admit the constant barrier, so strict domination applies. Letting ε decrease to zero proves global greatestness; the same comparison gives bounded-type uniqueness. These applications match [BGL, Section 4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.01090v1), with existence independently cross-checked against [Guedj–Lu, Theorem 3.4(1)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.01938), and the bounded maximum step against [Guedj–Lu, Lemma 1.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2106.04272).

The contraction estimates are correct. A common positive lower bound for Z, the displayed uniform bound B for A(w), and the derivative bound 2σB‖h‖∞ give the stated contraction constant. Its fixed point has a continuous complex Hessian. Local bounded Bedford–Taylor recursion, followed by mollification of that Hessian, identifies the actual residual product. Bidegrees permit exactly one horizontal and k vertical factors, yielding N bᵏAσ dW. This computation uses no formal power of the divisor current. The measure is positive and has mass at most N a max bᵏ.

Dominated convergence gives Aσ→aH/m in L¹ with a uniform density bound. The uniformly integrable logarithmic Green-kernel tail upgrades this to uniform convergence wσ→w₀. Consequently the whole normalized family converges in L¹ and locally uniformly off D to v₀=ψ+w₀−S₀. Its measure is computed directly as c₀f dW, rather than inferred from an unrestricted continuity theorem. Its bounded residual proves ordinary type φ. The competitors φ−tC establish the exact all-scale stretching definition, including common poles.

The order characterization is proved in precisely the separated sector claimed. Its critical inequality forces the horizontal non-pluripolar measure to dominate (aH/m)ω₁, whose mass is a. The entire positive closed curve current also has mass a. The degree-one non-pluripolar restriction therefore leaves no polar mass and forces equality of the entire current. The resulting distributional Poisson equation gives r=w₀+C canonically. Hence the mean constraint is exactly C≤−∫(ψ+w₀)dν₀, making s₀ the greatest admissible critical subsolution in that sector. Supremum normalization selects v₀ there. No uniqueness outside this sector is asserted or needed.

The scalar error is retained correctly. Writing L=∫H(ψ+w₀)ω₁, the dominated difference quotient gives (Zσ−m)/σ→L. Together with cσ=a e^{σSσ}/Zσ, this proves both σ⁻¹log(cσ/c₀)→S₀−L/m and sσ−σ⁻¹log c₀→ψ+w₀−L/m. The same integrable bounds work for moving parameters without a rate relation.

For the moving theorem, the uniform residual bound and dⱼ bounded away from zero keep all maximizing points away from D. Thus Sⱼ→S₀. Uniform convergence of bⱼ and L¹ convergence of Aⱼ give the claimed total-variation measure convergence. The explicit continuous residual profiles φⱼ−ψⱼ converge uniformly; together with dⱼ→d and the explicit limiting potential, this proves actual limiting ordinary type. Type retention is therefore established independently of L¹ convergence. Centering by c₀,ⱼ=aⱼ/mⱼ is essential: replacing it by c₀ introduces the uncontrolled term σⱼ⁻¹log(c₀,ⱼ/c₀).

The example is admissible and nontrivial. For a=1, d=1/4, b=2+t and H=1, the centered limit is ψ+1/4 and the scalar-error limit is 1/4. With the stated Hopf surface factor, the product is non-Kähler and its limiting mass is 3∫(2+t)²ω₁=13. The descended Hermitian form and S¹×S³ topology are verified directly; the odd first Betti number excludes a Kähler metric. The proposed wrong-centering example indeed diverges to +∞.

Harmless wording clarifications are needed: the removal lemma should explicitly specify v∈PSH(X,θ), the domain already used in its proof and every application; and φⱼ−ψⱼ at D denotes the displayed continuous residual extension, not subtraction of two infinite values. BGL v1 Lemma 4.1 also has an intermediate variable typo: the maximum calculation concerns vε. Reconstructing that calculation verifies the comparison argument with this correction. None requires a new mathematical argument. Differences in ddᶜ conventions are positive rescalings and preserve the applications after the corresponding potential and exponent rescaling.

passages.statement: Let A be a closed pluripolar subset of a complex manifold U. Every genuine plurisubharmonic function on U\A that is locally bounded above near A has a unique canonical plurisubharmonic extension to U. (Demailly, I, Theorem 5.24.)
passages.quote: locally bounded above near A extends uniquely

passages.statement: For a family of plurisubharmonic functions on an open set that is locally uniformly bounded above, the upper semicontinuous regularization of its supremum is plurisubharmonic, or identically minus infinity on a component, and agrees almost everywhere with that supremum. (Demailly, I, Theorem 5.7.)

Mixed Bedford–Taylor products of locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions are positive, symmetric and defined by the recursive distributional formula. They converge weakly when all potential sequences decrease to locally bounded limits; they also converge under locally uniform convergence to finite continuous plurisubharmonic limits. (Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2; Demailly, III, Sections 3.A–3.B.)

Mixed Bedford–Taylor products of locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions are positive, symmetric and defined by the recursive distributional formula. They converge weakly when all potential sequences decrease to locally bounded limits; they also converge under locally uniform convergence to finite continuous plurisubharmonic limits. (Bedford–Taylor, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2; Demailly, III, Sections 3.A–3.B.)

Let ω be a smooth semipositive real (1,1)-form, not necessarily closed, and let u and v be bounded genuine ω-psh functions on an open set U. Their bounded Monge–Ampère products satisfy MAω(max(u,v)) ≥ 1_{u>v}MAω(u)+1_{u≤v}MAω(v), including the equality set in the second term. (Guedj–Lu, Quasi-plurisubharmonic envelopes 2, Lemma 1.2.)
passages.quote: Let u, v, ϕ be bounded ω-psh functions in U ⊆ X.

passages.statement: Let η be a smooth strictly positive Hermitian form on a connected compact complex manifold, let dV be a smooth strictly positive volume form, and let g≥0 be nonzero in Lᵖ(dV) for some p>1. For every σ>0 there is a unique bounded genuine η-psh solution of MAη(R)=e^{σR}g dV. This assertion does not require the bounded mass property. (Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Theorem 4.5, positive-background case; Guedj–Lu, Quasi-plurisubharmonic envelopes 3, Theorem 3.4(1).)

Let η be a smooth strictly positive Hermitian form on a connected compact complex manifold, let dV be a smooth strictly positive volume form, and let g≥0 be nonzero in Lᵖ(dV) for some p>1. For every σ>0 there is a unique bounded genuine η-psh solution of MAη(R)=e^{σR}g dV. This assertion does not require the bounded mass property. (Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Theorem 4.5, positive-background case; Guedj–Lu, Quasi-plurisubharmonic envelopes 3, Theorem 3.4(1).)

Let η be a smooth strictly positive Hermitian form on a compact complex manifold, and let u,v be bounded genuine η-psh functions. If 1_{u<v}MAη(u)≤q·1_{u<v}MAη(v) for a constant q∈[0,1), then u≥v everywhere. (Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Lemma 4.2, with a constant global strict barrier below both potentials.)

For genuine psh potentials with a smooth, possibly nonclosed background, bounded local products are defined using smooth-background correction terms. The associated finite-level non-pluripolar construction is plurifinely local, agrees with the bounded product on its bounded level sets, and assigns zero mass to pluripolar sets. These local properties require no bounded mass property and do not assert uniform global mass bounds. (Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Section 2.1, Proposition 2.1 and its construction.)

For a positive closed (1,1)-current T=β+ddᶜr on a complex curve, where β is smooth and r is a genuine β-psh potential, its degree-one non-pluripolar product is 1_{r>−∞}T. (Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi, Section 1.2.)
passages.quote: Condition (1.2) is always satisfied when p = 1

passages.statement: Every odd-degree Betti number of a compact Kähler manifold is even. (Demailly, VI, Corollary 8.3.)

A real distribution on an open subset of Euclidean space whose distributional Laplacian is a positive measure has a unique locally integrable canonical subharmonic representative. (Demailly, I, Theorem 4.20.)
